title: Data, knowledge & context
subtitle: Governed knowledge bases, retrieval lineage, the prompt registry, agent memory and context policies.

common.aclHint: Permission references (group / role / principal handles) — never credentials.
common.credentialWarning: That looks like a credential value. Enter a permission reference (a group / role / principal handle), never a secret.
common.localHashHint: This index uses a local lexical (hash) embedder, NOT a semantic vector model. Matches are keyword-based, not meaning-based.
common.egressNoHint: Data did not leave the perimeter.
common.egressYesHint: The wired embedder sent text to an external provider (recorded in lineage).
common.egressProviderHint: An opaque hash of the provider — never the provider name or value.
common.hashHint: A one-way hash — the underlying text is never stored or shown.
common.localOnlyHint: Zero-egress lock — no chunk text may leave the perimeter.

kbs.name: Knowledge base
kbs.emptyHint: Declare a knowledge base to ingest and govern retrieval over your content.
kbs.truncated: Loaded {{n}} knowledge bases; there are more
kbs.truncatedHint: There are more knowledge bases than shown; this page takes rows by id. One missing from this list does not prove it does not exist.

kbDetail.title: Knowledge base
kbDetail.documentsCaption: Metadata and provenance only — the document body is never exposed (it lives only as redacted chunks).
kbDetail.docsEmptyHint: Ingest from a registered connector or paste inline documents.
kbDetail.documentsTruncatedHint: This list shows the first loaded page; more documents in this knowledge base exist.

kbEditor.createBody: Declares a knowledge base and records the wired embedder. local_only forbids any egress; model_backed requires a semantic embedder. Recorded in the audit ledger under your identity.
kbEditor.editBody: Updates governance for “{{name}}”. Changing classification, residency or ACL changes what each identity can retrieve. embed_model and dimension stay as recorded at create. Audited under your identity.
kbEditor.name: Name
kbEditor.classificationHint: Drives which identities may retrieve from this KB.
kbEditor.residencyHint: Pins where this KB’s data may be processed.
kbEditor.embedPolicyHint: local_only = zero-egress lexical index. model_backed = semantic vector index via the governed provider. auto = pick by the wired embedder. The backend rejects an invalid policy/embedder combination (400).

kbRemove.title: Delete knowledge base?
kbRemove.body: Permanently deletes “{{name}}” and ALL its documents and indexed chunks in one transaction. This cannot be undone. Lineage history is retained as evidence.

ingest.title: Ingest content
ingest.body: Ingests content into “{{name}}”. Secrets / PII are redacted before indexing. On a model_backed KB, chunk text is embedded via the governed provider (egress is recorded in lineage).
ingest.sourceHint: The registered connector NAME to pull from — never a credential. Credentials are resolved server-side and never seen by this module.
ingest.bodyHint: The raw text to ingest. It is redacted then chunked server-side — only redacted chunks are stored, never the raw body.
ingest.doneSummary: {{documents}} document(s), {{chunks}} chunk(s) · {{redactions}} secret(s) redacted before indexing

reindex.title: Reindex pending chunks?
reindex.body: Re-embeds the pending chunks for “{{name}}” — chunks that failed to index during a partial ingest. This re-runs the embedder over those chunks only.

query.title: Governed retrieval
query.body: Runs a governed retrieval against “{{name}}” as the given agent. Results are filtered by that identity’s clearance, ACL and residency, and this query is recorded in the lineage (origin → answer).
query.queryHint: The retrieval query — this is hashed for lineage, never stored as text.
query.resultsCaption: Already permission-filtered server-side. Each chunk shows its redacted text, score, classification and provenance.
query.noResults: No chunks matched (or none were within your clearance).
query.noModeResults: No chunks match this source mode.
query.contextTruncated: ⛔ The context did not fit: {{n}} chunks were dropped. This answer was built on less evidence than the list below suggests.
query.excludedChunks: {{n}} chunks excluded by the source floor ({{sources}})

lineage.selfAudited: Viewing the data lineage is itself logged (self-audited): each list and open writes an audit event.
lineage.emptyHint: Lineage rows are appended as governed retrievals run.
lineage.chunkRefsCaption: Origin → answer evidence — references and hashes only, never text.
lineage.truncated: Loaded {{n}} lineage records; there are more
lineage.truncatedHint: The lineage trail is longer than this page. A record missing here does not prove the access never happened.

prompts.name: Prompt
prompts.emptyHint: Register a prompt to version its template with an immutable history.
prompts.revisionsCaption: Immutable, newest-first revisions. Templates shown are redacted (secret examples removed).
prompts.label: Label
prompts.truncatedHint: There are more prompts than shown; this page takes rows by id. One missing from this list does not prove it is not published.

promptEditor.createBody: Creates the prompt and stores its first revision. The template is redacted (secret examples removed) before storage. Audited under your identity.
promptEditor.addBody: Appends a new immutable revision to “{{name}}” and makes it current. The previous revision is kept (history is immutable). The template is redacted before storage. Audited under your identity.
promptEditor.name: Name
promptEditor.templateHint: Secret-looking values are redacted server-side before storage — do not paste real credentials.
promptEditor.label: Label

rollback.title: Roll back prompt?
rollback.body: Moves the active pointer of “{{name}}” to revision {{rev}}. No revision is deleted — history stays immutable.

memory.caption: Governed agent memory. Content is redacted before storage; expired entries are filtered on read.
memory.emptyHint: Write a memory entry for an agent, or filter by an agent ref.
memory.withheld: ⛔ {{n}} entries are NOT in this list: the read path withheld them because they failed the integrity check. The list is not the whole picture, and what is missing is what most needs looking at — run the memory verification to see them.

memoryEditor.title: Write memory
memoryEditor.body: Upserts a memory entry for the given agent under the given key. Content is redacted before storage; a TTL sets an expiry. Audited under your identity.
memoryEditor.contentHint: Secret-looking values are redacted server-side before storage.
memoryEditor.ttlHint: Optional — > 0 sets an expiry; expired entries are never returned.

memoryRemove.title: Delete memory entry?
memoryRemove.body: Deletes this memory entry for the agent. This cannot be undone.

memoryPurge.title: Purge expired memory?
memoryPurge.body: Materializes expiry: deletes expired memory entries{{agentSuffix}}. This cannot be undone.

context.caption: Context / compaction policies. Applies these at model-call time — this view governs the data only.
context.emptyHint: Upsert a policy to govern how a scope’s context is composed and compacted.

contextEditor.title: Upsert context policy
contextEditor.body: Sets the context policy for {{scopeKind}}:{{scopeRef}}. This governs how that scope’s context is composed / compacted and whether redaction is required. Audited under your identity.

lifecycle.deprecateHint: Mark as deprecated. Data is still served with a warning.

dlp.enabled: DLP is enabled: a labelled class with no exact rule falls to the "*" rule, and with no "*" rule it is DENIED.
dlp.inert: DLP is NOT configured — the gate is inert and nothing is being blocked. This is not "everything denied".
dlp.unscannedDenied: Unscanned content is DENIED: it has no label, so its sensitivity cannot be proved.
dlp.unscannedAllowed: Unscanned content is ALLOWED by an explicit rule. Content nobody classified can leave.
dlp.unscannedUndetermined: Cannot be determined from this page — the rule list is truncated, so a rule allowing unscanned content may exist beyond it.
dlp.emptyHint: With no rules the gate does not enforce. Writing one rule enables DLP for this tenant.
dlp.anyScope: matches any LABELLED class — it does NOT cover unscanned content
dlp.newRuleHint: A rule binds one content class to allow or deny on egress.
dlp.willReplace: ⛔ A rule for "{{class}}" already exists. Saving REPLACES it — this is an upsert by class, not an addition. Replacing a deny with an allow opens egress for that class immediately.
dlp.mayReplace: The rule list is truncated: a rule for "{{class}}" may already exist beyond this page. Saving would REPLACE it, because saving upserts by class.
dlp.truncated: Loaded {{n}} DLP rules; there are more
dlp.truncatedHint: This list shows the first loaded page; more DLP rules exist.

integrity.scope: Each live row's hash is recomputed and compared with its anchor in the signed ledger. This proves a live row against the chain; it does NOT prove absence.
integrity.truncated: The COUNTS above are complete; this detail list is capped. A short list does not mean few problems.

scans.scanSourceHint: Reads the source WITHOUT ingesting it. Bodies are classified in memory and never stored, logged or embedded.
scans.basisNotice: A scan records what it looked AT. "stored" is the post-scrub form kept after ingestion; "raw" is the body before redaction. The two are not comparable.
scans.zeroOnStored: ⛔ Zero hits here means the redaction worked, NOT that the corpus holds no sensitive data — anything scrubbed at ingestion is already gone. Scan the SOURCE to ask that question.
scans.zeroOnRaw: Zero hits on the raw bodies: the source itself carried nothing the detectors recognise.
scans.truncatedHint: This list shows the first loaded page; more scan records exist.

portability.title: Portability
portability.excluded: ⛔ {{n}} entries were LEFT OUT because they failed the integrity check. This bundle is not a complete copy — say so if you hand it to a data subject.
portability.noManifest: The bundle carries no readable manifest, so its completeness cannot be stated.
portability.rejectedCount: {{n}} rows were REJECTED individually. The import partly succeeded — these rows are not in.
